M1.desc: For every family, the kaleidoscope shape of any seed is the Minkowski sum of the corner shapes, weighted by the seed's barycentric coordinates (support functions agree)
M1.detail: 7 families A3 B3 H3 A4 B4 F4 H4, random seeds, 2000 directions each, max error 5.3e-15

M2.desc: Along the depth path, the shape at depth k + f is (1 - f)·corner_k + f·corner_(k+1), Minkowski sum, up to size
M2.detail: A3 B3 H3 B4 F4, 9 depths each, max error 2.8e-15

M3.desc: The lemma behind M1: when the seed and the direction both lie in the chamber, the identity wins the maximum, so the support function is linear in the seed (Kostant convexity, standard)
M3.detail: 6 families, 20 random pairs each, max error 1.1e-16

H1.desc: Face side: the same shape is the intersection of the corner shapes' polars, each scaled by the ratio <seed, corner> (cube ∩ scaled octahedron = truncated cube)
H1.detail: A3 B3 H3 A4 B4 F4, random seeds, max radial error 1.2e-14

O1.desc: The depth fraction f is the chance reading t/(1 + t) of an odds t = f/(1 - f) between two corners

O2.desc: Resizing the corner shapes changes no shape, only multiplies the odds by a fixed factor (a Bayes factor): depth fractions depend on a size convention, odds ratios do not
O2.detail: corners scaled 2 and 0.5, odds 3/7 -> 1.7143, same shape (ratio spread 4.4e-16)

O3.desc: The odds complement 1/t is the mirror of the depth path (f -> 1 - f)

O4.desc: Equal odds on every corner of the simplex family give the permutohedron: Perm(n) = Δ(1,n) + Δ(2,n) + … + Δ(n,n), the hypersimplices summed

G1.desc: The associahedron (not a kaleidoscope shape) is a Minkowski sum of simplex faces with odds 1 each (Postnikov 2009; Loday 2004)

G2.desc: Every zonotope is a weighted Minkowski sum of segments

I1.desc: For 1 < p < ∞ every face-power shape is strictly convex: the Hessian of Σ|a + n_i·x|^p is a positive sum of n_i n_iᵀ and the normals span, so no flat facet exists and no finite p gives a polytope
I1.detail: 5 solids, p = 1.5, 3, 10, 40: normals rank 3 for all, smallest face value on the boundary 6.28e-05 > 0

I2.desc: No setting of p on any listed solid gives an in-between (truncated) depth shape: p in (1, ∞) is strictly convex (I1), p = ∞ gives the solid itself, and p = 1 gives the polar of a zonotope, whose faces are centrally symmetric, while every truncation's polar has triangular faces
I2.detail: p = 1 bodies: tetrahedron -> 12 corners, 14 faces; cube -> 6 corners, 8 faces; octahedron -> 12 corners, 14 faces; icosahedron -> 90 corners, 92 faces; dodecahedron -> 30 corners, 32 faces; cuboctahedron -> 18 corners, 32 faces; icosidodecahedron -> 90 corners, 152 faces

I3.desc: But p = 1 does land on some whole-depth shapes (a crossing, not containment): it gives the polar of a zonotope, and three of those are kaleidoscope shapes (cube -> octahedron, octahedron -> cuboctahedron, dodecahedron -> icosidodecahedron)
I3.detail: tetrahedron at p = 1 has the combinatorics of B3 depth 1; cube at p = 1 has the combinatorics of A3 depth 1, B3 depth 2; octahedron at p = 1 has the combinatorics of B3 depth 1; dodecahedron at p = 1 has the combinatorics of H3 depth 1

I4.desc: Depth never reaches a rounded shape: every depth shape is a polytope (the convex hull of a finite orbit), while p = 2 is a ball for every shape
I4.detail: by construction; checked in W2 of checks.py that p = 2 is round

I5.desc: Odds on all corners reach shapes no depth setting reaches: equal odds on the cube family's three corners give the truncated cuboctahedron (48 corners), off every depth path (24 corners at most)
I5.detail: omnitruncation 48 corners; depth path at most 24

S1.desc: Face-power on the triangle at p = 2 is exactly a circle (the circumscribed one)

S2.desc: The temperature route is never exactly a circle at finite β: on any circle its function has a cos 3θ term with coefficient 6·I₃(βρ) > 0 (Bessel), so a level set cannot be a circle
S2.detail: I₃(z) > 0 for all z > 0 (series with positive terms); checked on 200 values 1e-4..1e3

S3.desc: Measured: the temperature boundary's 3-fold content is nonzero at every β, hot or cold

S4.desc: At the triangle's own offset the two routes are different families: at equal 3-fold content their 6-fold content differs, so no change of speed turns one into the other
S4.detail: largest 6-fold gap 4.48e-03 at matched 3-fold content, over 58 matched pairs

S5.desc: Exact in one limit only: face-power with offset a and p = β·a tends to the temperature shape as a → ∞, error falling like 1/a ((1 + y/a)^(βa) → e^(βy))
